recipe_version.title: Jamaican Jerk Pork Chops with Pineapple Slaw
recipe_version.description: Bone-in pork chops coated in a blended Scotch-bonnet jerk paste, skillet-seared, served with crunchy pineapple-cabbage slaw.

ingredients.name: bone-in pork chops
ingredients.note: about 8 oz each, 3/4 to 1 inch thick

ingredients.name: Scotch bonnet pepper
ingredients.note: seeded for hot-but-not-nuclear; leave seeds for hotter. Wear gloves.

ingredients.name: ground allspice
ingredients.note: required jerk spice; not pumpkin-pie blend

ingredients.name: tamari
ingredients.note: soy allergen. Tamari so wheat is not introduced. All of it goes into the jerk paste.

ingredients.name: lime juice
ingredients.note: from about 1 lime; more lime for the slaw listed separately

ingredients.name: olive oil
ingredients.note: 2 tbsp in the paste, 1 tbsp for the skillet

ingredients.name: kosher salt
ingredients.note: 1 tsp in the paste, 1/4 tsp on the slaw

ingredients.name: lime
ingredients.note: juice for the slaw (about 2 tbsp); zest optional fine grate into slaw

steps.title: Make the jerk paste
steps.body: In a blender or mini food processor, combine the scallions, thyme leaves, garlic, ginger, Scotch bonnet, ground allspice, cinnamon, nutmeg, brown sugar, tamari, 2 tbsp lime juice, 2 tbsp olive oil, 1 tsp kosher salt, and black pepper. Blend to a thick, spoonable paste, about 30 to 60 seconds, scraping once. Wear gloves when handling the Scotch bonnet.

steps.title: Coat the chops
steps.body: Pat the pork chops dry. Rub all of the jerk paste over both sides of the 4 chops. Rest at room temperature 15 minutes while you make the slaw. Do not rinse the paste off.

steps.title: Make the pineapple slaw
steps.body: In a large bowl, toss the shredded green cabbage, diced pineapple, julienned red bell pepper, chopped cilantro, juice of 1 lime (about 2 tbsp), and the remaining 1/4 tsp kosher salt. Taste; the slaw should be bright and crunchy, not watery. Hold at room temperature while the chops cook.

steps.title: Sear the jerk chops
steps.body: Heat the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium heat. Add the chops in a single layer. Cook until the first side is deep brown with spice crust, about 5 to 6 minutes. Flip. Cook the second side until an instant-read thermometer in the thickest part away from bone reads 145 F, about 5 to 7 minutes more. If the paste darkens too fast, lower to medium-low. Do not char to bitter black.

steps.title: Rest and plate
steps.body: Transfer chops to a plate. Rest 5 minutes. Plate one chop per person with a mound of pineapple slaw beside it. Spoon any skillet juices over the pork. No second sauce. kitchen_tested is false.

recipe_version.heat: Medium skillet for the chops; lower to medium-low if the paste threatens to burn. No oven.
recipe_version.doneness: Pork chops 145 F in the thickest part away from bone, then 5-minute rest. Paste deep brown, not bitter black. Slaw crunchy. kitchen_tested is false.

curator_preflight.detail: All paste ingredients blend in step 1. Oil split 2 tbsp paste / 1 tbsp skillet. Salt split 1 tsp paste / 1/4 tsp slaw. Two lime uses: 2 tbsp in paste and 1 lime juiced for slaw.
3 tbsp olive oil total, fully accounted.
Jerk paste is blended from listed aromatics and spices, not a bottled jerk sauce. Pineapple slaw is built in the bowl.
Prep 20 (paste + shred slaw veg) + cook 32 (15 rest with paste on while slaw finishes + 12 sear + 5 rest) = 52. Slaw work overlaps the 15-minute paste rest.
Scotch bonnet does not quarter; use a small piece for 1–2. Thermometer target 145 F does not scale.
